subject: science
passage: When a person is cold or frightened, tiny muscles at the base of the body's hairs contract, pulling each hair upright and raising the skin around it into the small bumps commonly called goosebumps. In a furred mammal the same reflex serves a purpose: fluffed fur traps a thicker layer of air against the skin in cold weather, and a cat or dog that bristles looks larger to a rival. Humans have kept the reflex while losing nearly all of the fur, so that the response is now ______, a remnant that still fires on cue but accomplishes nothing the body needs. That it persists at all is a reminder that evolution removes only what it is pressed to remove.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The appositive after the comma defines the blank: "a remnant that still fires on cue but accomplishes nothing the body needs." A trait that survives from an ancestor but has lost its function is "vestigial." The contrast with the furred mammal, in which "the same reflex serves a purpose," confirms that the human version is a functionless leftover.
explanation.A: Correct. "Vestigial" describes a structure or behavior retained from ancestors that no longer serves its original function, exactly what the appositive describes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The reflex is involuntary, but that is true of the furred mammal's useful reflex too; the blank must capture what changed in humans, the loss of function.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Atavistic" describes an ancestral trait that reappears after having been lost. The text says humans "have kept the reflex"; it never disappeared.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Adaptive" means useful for survival. The text says the human reflex "accomplishes nothing the body needs."
